# crosswork_provider_profiles (Resource)

This resource can manage a provider profile.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "crosswork_provider_profiles" "example" {
  name    = "cwtest-provider-profiles"
  family  = "ROBOT_PROVIDER_NSO"
  profile = "cwtest-provider-profile"
  connectivity = [
    {
      protocol   = "ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_SSH"
      ip_address = "192.0.2.50"
      port       = 22
      timeout    = 60
    }
  ]
  supported_models = [
    {
      model_prefix  = "Cisco-IOS-XR"
      model_version = "7.8.2"
    }
  ]
  properties = { nso_crosslaunch_url = "https://nso.example.invalid/nso" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connectivity` (Attributes List) Connections to the provider, one per protocol; each uses an IP address or an FQDN (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--connectivity))
- `family` (String) Provider family; the controller stores the SR PCE family of the Add Provider form as `ROBOT_PROVIDER_XTC`
  - Choices: `ROBOT_PROVIDER_NSO`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_EPNM`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_WAE`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_CSM`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_XTC`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_SYSLOG_STORAGE`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_SR_PCE`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_ALERT`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_DESTINATION`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_OPTIMA`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_PROXY`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_ONC`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_ACCEDIAN_PROXY`, `ROBOT_PROVIDER_CROSSWORK_AI`
- `name` (String) Provider name, unique on the Crosswork cluster
- `profile` (String) Name of the credential profile, which must hold a username and password for every protocol the provider uses

### Optional

- `certificate_name` (String) Name of the certificate profile of the provider, required by some families (Accedian proxy) and checked to exist
- `instance` (String) Select an instance of the provider configuration by its name. Leave it unset to use the default instance.
- `properties` (Map of String) Provider properties such as `nso_crosslaunch_url`, `embedded_nso` or `webui-root-resource`, as key and value
- `supported_models` (Attributes List) Device models the provider supports, required for the NSO family (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--supported_models))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id of the object

<a id="nestedatt--connectivity"></a>
### Nested Schema for `connectivity`

Required:

- `port` (Number) Port
  - Range: `1`-`65535`
- `protocol` (String) Protocol
  - Choices: `ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_SSH`, `ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_NETCONF`, `ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_HTTP`, `ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_HTTPS`, `ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_TCP`, `ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_GRPC`, `ROBOT_MSVC_TRANS_GNMI`

Optional:

- `encoding_type` (String) Encoding of a gNMI or gRPC connection, required for the gNMI protocol
  - Choices: `JSON`, `BYTES`, `PROTO`, `ASCII`, `JSON_IETF`, `XML`, `YANG`
- `fqdn_domain_name` (String) Domain name part of the FQDN of the provider
- `fqdn_host_name` (String) Host name part of the FQDN of the provider; leave it unset when `ip_address` is used
- `ip_address` (String) IPv4 address of the provider; leave it unset when `fqdn_host_name` is used
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout in seconds, the controller uses 30 when it is not set


<a id="nestedatt--supported_models"></a>
### Nested Schema for `supported_models`

Required:

- `model_prefix` (String) Model prefix
  - Choices: `Cisco-IOS-XR`, `Cisco-NX-OS`, `Cisco-IOS-XE`
- `model_version` (String) Model version

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import crosswork_provider_profiles.example "<name>"
```
